The Opportunity
Join Hitachi Energy as the Quality & Continuous Improvement Leader for North America
, where you will lead an integrated Quality and Continuous Improvement organization focused on improving customer outcomes and overall business performance.
This is an opportunity for an experienced business and operations leader who has successfully used Quality and Continuous Improvement to transform performance. You will establish the governance, operating discipline, process architecture, and improvement capabilities needed to make significant problems visible, prevent quality escapes, and strengthen execution before process deterioration becomes a customer, operational, or financial failure.
This position is broader than traditional Quality Management System administration. The successful candidate will bring substantial operational leadership experience, strong Quality and Continuous Improvement knowledge, and the credibility to challenge and influence senior leaders across Engineering, Project Management, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field Service, Product Management, Operations, and other global functions.
How You’ll Make an Impact
Deploy the North American Quality and Continuous Improvement strategy, priorities, governance model, and operating rhythm in alignment with customer requirements, business objectives, and operational priorities.
Build and lead a high-performing, integrated Q&CI organization with clear accountabilities, strong functional leadership, appropriate succession depth, and the competencies required to govern quality events and drive systemic improvement.
Develop leaders and teams who combine technical knowledge, operational judgment, structured problem-solving, and cross-functional influence.
Establish and maintain the business Quality Management System, including effective governance of nonconformance reports, Customer Complaint Resolution Process, transactional Net Promoter Score, customer escalations, audits, certifications, and other critical quality systems.
Ensure significant quality issues are visible, assigned to accountable owners, appropriately escalated, aged transparently, and driven through verified closure.
Strengthen organizational problem-solving capability using root-cause analysis, 8D, corrective and preventive actions, creation-point and escape-point analysis, exposure assessment, recurrence prevention, and verification of effectiveness.
Ensure quality investigations follow failure mechanisms across organizational and functional boundaries, including Projects, Engineering, Suppliers, Product, factories, Research and Development, and global functions.
Strengthen project, supplier, engineering, and product-quality capabilities, including quality planning, engineering controls, supplier quality, factory acceptance testing, field execution, and lessons learned.
Provide effective quality oversight, challenge, and assurance for product reliability and fitness for purpose while maintaining accountability with the appropriate business and technical owners.
Develop strong interfaces with global Product, factory, R&D, Quality, Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain organizations to ensure North American customer and business issues receive effective ownership and resolution.
Lead the development and maintenance of the end-to-end business process landscape and its governance framework.
Partner with business-appointed process owners to clarify process ownership, interfaces, controls, performance expectations, and accountability.
Establish a methodology for mission-based key performance indicators and support process owners in defining measures tied to intended process outcomes.
Provide analytical support and methodology for developing nested leading indicators and effective process controls that identify deterioration before failure occurs.
Use quality, customer, and operating-performance data to identify systemic improvement opportunities and recommend cross-functional Continuous Improvement priorities.
Facilitate business-sponsored improvement initiatives while ensuring named business owners remain accountable for implementation, benefits realization, and sustainment.
Connect Quality and Continuous Improvement performance to measurable business outcomes, including customer satisfaction, delivery, project margin, working capital, productivity, predictability, and profitability.
Build a culture of transparency, accountability, structured problem-solving, and continuous improvement while ensuring functional organizations retain ownership for the quality and performance of their work.
Your Background
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Quality, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Significant leadership experience within an engineered-products, project-based, manufacturing, infrastructure, or industrial-services organization.
Demonstrated P&L, operating-unit, or substantial operational responsibility with accountability for customer outcomes, delivery, cost, margin, working capital, productivity, or overall business performance.
Broad practical experience across several of the following functions: Engineering, Project Management, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field Service, Product Management, Quality, and Continuous Improvement.
Proven success using Quality and Continuous Improvement to achieve measurable improvements in customer satisfaction, delivery, cost, project margin, working capital, productivity, predictability, or profitability.
Experience leading cross-functional transformation in complex regional and global organizations.
Strong working knowledge of nonconformance management, root-cause analysis, 8D, corrective and preventive actions, escape analysis, recurrence prevention, effectiveness verification, process measures, and leading indicators.
Demonstrated ability to distinguish immediate symptoms from underlying business, technical, and process causes.
Experience establishing or improving an end-to-end process landscape, clarifying process ownership, and strengthening interfaces across functional boundaries.
Demonstrated ability to use mission-based KPIs, leading indicators, and process controls to identify deterioration and enable action before failure occurs.
Proven ability to lead systemic improvement across processes that extend beyond individual corrective-action or preventive-action activities.
Experience building organizations, developing leaders, strengthening functional competencies, establishing accountability, and sustaining organizational change.
Executive-level communication and escalation skills, with the credibility to challenge and influence senior functional and operational leaders without relying on direct authority.
A leadership style that combines transparency, accountability, practical business judgment, systems thinking, structured problem-solving, and continuous improvement.

Senior Director, Continuous Improvement
Catalent
Harmans, MD
Senior Director of Continuous Improvement
Position Summary:
100% on-site in Harmans, MD
Catalent’s Baltimore facility is a leading center for biologics development and manufacturing, offering state-of-the-art capabilities in clinical and commercial supply. The site supports a wide range of services, including process development, drug substance manufacturing, and aseptic fill/finish for biologics and advanced therapies. With a strong focus on innovation and quality, the Baltimore location plays a key role in delivering life-changing treatments to patients worldwide. Team members here work in a collaborative environment that values expertise, precision, and continuous improvement, making it an exciting place to contribute to cutting-edge biopharmaceutical solutions.
The Senior Director, Continuous Improvement (C.I.) is the senior transformation leader for the Maryland sites. This role is accountable for building the site operating system, aligning the leadership team around the highest value business priorities, and converting strategy into disciplined execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and client commitments. This leader is not limited to leading improvement projects. The role functions as an enterprise change leader and Chief of Staff partner to the General Manager, translating site strategy into governance, routines, metrics, accountability, and sustained behavioral change across functions.
The role will lead operational transformation through lean, six sigma, daily management, strategy deployment, problem solving, value stream improvement, digital enablement, and disciplined change management. The emphasis is on building the management system that makes improvement repeatable, measurable, and owned by the business. By strengthening execution and decision making, this role will contribute to Catalent's Patient First philosophy by helping the Maryland sites reliably deliver high quality medicines to clients and patients with speed, compliance, and financial discipline.
The Role:
Serve as the senior site transformation leader, partnering with the General Manager and SLT to define and execute the transformation strategy, governance model, operating cadence, and enterprise-aligned priorities.
Build and sustain a site operating system that integrates strategy deployment, daily management, tiered accountability, visual performance management, KPI ownership, and disciplined execution.
Lead cross-functional transformation initiatives across Manufacturing, Quality, MSAT, Supply Chain, Engineering, Facilities, Finance, and support functions to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, compliance, and customer outcomes.
Translate business objectives into a prioritized portfolio of improvement initiatives with defined ownership, milestones, value realization, risk management, and governance structures.
Act as a strategic Chief of Staff to the General Manager by leading executive reviews, leadership routines, decision forums, communications, and action tracking to accelerate site performance.
Develop and manage a site-wide transformation scorecard, providing a single source of truth for performance metrics, value capture, risk mitigation, and recovery planning.
Drive operational excellence through advanced problem-solving and continuous improvement focused on deviations, right-first-time performance, cycle time, capacity, productivity, inventory optimization, and cost performance.
Coach and develop leaders and teams in Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, standard work, value stream thinking, daily management, and sustainable change leadership practices.
Embed standardized ways of working, governance processes, accountability mechanisms, and continuous improvement behaviors that deliver lasting organizational impact beyond individual projects.
Lead and develop the Continuous Improvement organization while partnering with global, regional, and Cell & Gene Therapy leadership to align transformation efforts, share best practices, and maximize business results.
Other duties as assigned.

Bachelor's degree with an emphasis in Life Science, Engineering, Business, Operations, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
A minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience leading operational excellence, transformation, strategy deployment, or business system implementation in complex manufacturing or technical operations.
Experience leading enterprise or site level transformation in GMP manufacturing, biologics, cell therapy, gene therapy, sterile manufacturing, pharmaceutical operations, or similarly regulated environments.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a senior leader and trusted partner to a General Manager or site head, including executive governance, operating reviews, decision support, and cross functional accountability.
Proven experience building or maturing a management system, daily management system, production system, or business operating system across multiple functions.
Certification in Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, Master Black Belt, Lean, Operational Excellence, or equivalent demonstrated capability. Deep understanding of lean, six sigma, daily management, tiered escalation, strategy deployment, standard work, visual management, value stream improvement, and benefits realization.
Track record delivering measurable business results through transformation, including quality, delivery, productivity, cost, inventory, compliance, cycle time, or client performance improvements.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect operational performance to financial outcomes, client commitments, capacity, working capital, labor productivity, and site competitiveness.
